objective: Migrate the legacy Android Telnyx Meet sample into a maintainable Compose Multiplatform application with shared presentation and domain code, coroutine-based state and effects, and platform-specific Telnyx video adapters for Android and iOS.
expected_outcomes: The fork contains a buildable Kotlin Multiplatform project with shared Compose UI and navigation.
Shared networking, repositories, use cases, presentation state, and events use structured Kotlin coroutines and Flow.
Android and iOS integrate their native Telnyx video SDKs behind one capability-aware shared meeting contract.
The existing Android sample's supported meeting workflows remain available and iOS capability gaps are explicit rather than simulated.
The migration is independently tested, reviewed, integrated, and reproducible from a clean checkout.
included_scope: Gradle and module migration to Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform
Shared Compose screens and navigation for room discovery, room creation, room join, meeting controls, participants, chat, and observable meeting state
Shared models, Ktor networking, serialization, repositories, use cases, reducers or presentation models, and validation
Kotlin suspend APIs, StateFlow for durable UI state, SharedFlow or channels for bounded one-off effects, cancellation, and structured concurrency
Android Telnyx video SDK adapter and Android permission, lifecycle, audio, camera, and screen-share integration
iOS TelnyxVideoSdk adapter through supported Objective-C/CocoaPods interop, plus iOS permission, lifecycle, audio, and camera integration
Capability-aware handling for SDK features that are unavailable on a platform
Common, Android, and iOS tests; architecture and dependency guards; CI for supported build targets
Removal of tracked local credentials and replacement with documented environment or local configuration
excluded_scope: Publishing to Google Play or the Apple App Store
Changing the public Telnyx SDK APIs or repositories
Pushing commits or branches to team-telnyx/telnyx-meet-android
Changing main in either the fork or upstream repository
A visual redesign unrelated to adopting shared Compose UI
Production credentials, production rooms, or destructive external operations
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout exposes commonMain, commonTest, androidMain, androidUnitTest, iosMain, and iosTest source sets and builds the supported Android and iOS targets with documented commands.
Shared Compose UI and navigation render the core room and meeting workflows without importing Android or UIKit classes from commonMain.
Shared asynchronous APIs are suspend-based or Flow-based; production common code contains no LiveData, Retrofit Callback, GlobalScope, or unmanaged CoroutineScope creation.
Screen state is represented by StateFlow and one-off effects have explicit buffered delivery and lifecycle cancellation semantics.

Android and iOS meeting engines implement the same shared contract and publish explicit capability state for camera, microphone, participants, chat, screen sharing, active speaker, and network statistics.
Existing supported Android behaviors are preserved or their intentional changes are documented and covered by tests; unsupported iOS behaviors are disabled with honest UI and tests.
Common unit tests, Android unit or instrumentation tests, iOS simulator tests, architecture checks, static analysis, and repository CI pass from a clean environment.
The dependency graph resolves without relying on the unavailable legacy WebRTC/libyuv artifacts observed at the base commit.

Tracked credential-bearing local.properties and equivalent secret files are removed from version control, ignored, and replaced by secret-free examples or documentation without exposing historical values.
Every accepted change is reviewed, tied to immutable evidence, and integrated only into kmp-fast-vm-test on the fork.
The final evidence proves upstream and both main branches were not mutated.
The final repository includes an architecture overview, platform capability matrix, build instructions, test instructions, and migration notes.
evidence_requirements: Clean-checkout Gradle build logs for common, Android, and iOS targets
Test reports for common, Android, iOS, architecture, and integration gates
Static scan proving forbidden platform imports and unstructured coroutine constructs are absent from common production code
Dependency-resolution report showing the legacy unavailable artifacts are not required
Secret scan and git-index evidence proving local credentials are untracked
Platform capability matrix linked to adapter tests
Candidate, review, conflict, CI, merge, cost, and FastVM cleanup receipts
Git evidence proving all writes stayed on the fork's kmp-fast-vm-test branch
